key_insight: A stationary 1/f noise emerges when a system is bounded by two fixed frequencies and has no other constant parameter besides the mean amplitude, leading to 1/f scaling in the intermediate range.
engineering_relevance: This gives a general, system-independent criterion for identifying or designing processes that produce broadband flicker noise in fluid, diffusion, and other engineering systems.
method: Analytically studied the ordinary diffusion equation.
Compared the derived spectrum with known scaling behavior in fluid turbulence.
Used the result to infer a necessary-and-sufficient condition for stationary 1/f noise.
evidence_signal: The paper’s evidence is analytical rather than experimental: it derives a diffusion-equation example and uses it to establish the frequency-boundary condition for 1/f behavior.
watch_item: The condition applies to stationary noise with clear low/high cutoff frequencies; real systems with nonstationarity, finite data windows, or extra controlling parameters may deviate from ideal 1/f scaling.
paper_title: Condition for $1/f$ noise to occur along with an example for a diffusion equation
